answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs, with deposits slashed when independent audits confirm fraud. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so multiplying accounts ties up capital and creates measurable loss risk rather than merely changing usernames. For example, cedar, lagoon, and quill could be registered names, but none grants influence without its own bonded stake; honest agents can recover theirs by behaving correctly.
